newsitem.title: JAPAN: Fujimori defends decision to raid residence.
newsitem.headline: Fujimori defends decision to raid residence.

text.p: Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori does not regret storming the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima to end the hostage crisis there, Japanese media reported on Monday.
In reports of a news conference Fujimori gave to Japanese reporters in Lima on Saturday, Fujimori said Japan was "idealistic" in hoping the siege could have been ended peacefully.
"Japan believed the residence was like an impenetrable fortress. We thought the Japanese government would reject our plan as not plausible if we consulted them in advance," Fujimori said.
"Japan's call for a peaceful resolution was idealistic and did not offer concrete suggestions," he added.
In the reports, carried by all major Japanese newspapers, Fujimori sidestepped accusations that some of the rebels who took over the embassy were executed in the rescue mission.
"The order was to save the 72 hostages...anything could happen under those circumstances, in the midst of a battle," Fujimori said.
All but one of the 72 hostages held in the residence since December, were rescued alive by Peruvian army and navy commandos last Tuesday in a daring military strike that killed all 14 hostage-takers.
The rebels, members of the Marxist Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA), had demanded the release of jailed comrades.
"If anyone in Japan defends the Tupac Amaru, please let me know. We have 2,000 dangerous Tupac members in Peruvian prisons and we can export them," Fujimori said.
